title: MAIA: Multi-Agent Intent Articulation for Requirement Discovery in Art Commissions
abstract: arXiv:2609.12097v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In bespoke art commissions, laypeople know what they feel but lack the words to specify it: one participant wanted a laid-off truck driver depicted as "a ghost in his own machine" but left the medium, scale, and palette unsaid. We frame this as an articulation bottleneck at an under-served upstream stage: requirement discovery, which precedes any artist or image generator and forces the commissioner to constitute intent in the first place. We present MAIA (Multi-Agent Intent Articulation), a multi-agent system that scaffolds this stage through Socratic inquiry under a "Verification over Invention" rule, turning vague affect into a text-only brief of visual terms the user verifies. In a within-subjects study (N = 16), the full configuration produced a large, significant gain in Cognitive Support over a minimal baseline (r = 0.97, p_FDR = 0.003; LMM p_FDR < 0.001). Thematic analysis traces the same mechanism, and a validator gate

translated_title: MAIA：面向艺术委托需求发现的多智能体意图表达系统
translated_abstract: 在定制艺术委托中，外行人知道自己感受到什么，却缺乏语言来明确表达：一位参与者希望将一名下岗卡车司机描绘成“自己机器中的幽灵”，却没有说明媒介、尺寸和色调。我们将此框定为需求发现这一长期被忽视的上游环节的表达瓶颈——该环节先于任何艺术家或图像生成器，迫使委托人首先构建自己的意图。我们提出了MAIA（多智能体意图表达），这是一个多智能体系统，在“验证优先于发明”规则下通过苏格拉底式提问来支撑这一阶段，将模糊的情感转化为用户可验证的纯文本视觉术语简报。在一项被试内研究（N = 16）中，完整配置相比最小基线在认知支持方面产生了大幅且显著的提升（r = 0.97, p_FDR = 0.003; LMM p_FDR < 0.001）。主题分析揭示了相同的机制，验证器关卡……
tldr: MAIA是一个多智能体系统，通过苏格拉底式提问和“验证优先于发明”规则，帮助艺术委托中的外行客户将模糊的情感意图表达为可验证的视觉术语简报，实验证明其在认知支持方面显著优于基线。
en_tdlr: MAIA is a multi-agent system that scaffolds requirement discovery in art commissions through Socratic inquiry under a "Verification over Invention" rule, turning laypeople's vague affect into user-verifiable text-only visual briefs with significant cognitive support gains over baseline.
